questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always been fascinated with the country to which i travelled. Also, the weather is much better and I had an opportunity to combine sunshine culture with academic learning which is very different from Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
California is extremely expensive which limits your opportunities. Furthermore, UCSD seemed extremely indifferent about the international students, we didn't get an introduction to anything, basically landed on Jan 4th and started school on jan 7th without introductions to classes, systems or enrollment. 
San Diego is a great city though, and the overall quality of life is high there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really difficult. Felt like there was a big gap between UC and KU.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was no help what so ever. I had an online 45 min course with 3 students talking about their lives. Non-school related mostly. That was it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Please do some sort of introduction to the system. People land 3 days before school starts due to quarter structure which means you can't even get into it once you're there before you start classes.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay. Look around on the internet and write plenty of people!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you go to UCSD, live off campus! San Diego is an awesome city, and campus is far away from the 'city' which means you won't experience as much of the city itself if you live on campus. Also, campus housing is extremely expensive. Futhermore, the school 'spirit' really is not there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be prepared to fork out some money.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: no help with this. Also registration only started to work 4 days before I landed in San Diego.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You use WebReg to sign up and EASy to get pre-reqs approved so you can take non-introduction courses. Be aware that the first 2 weeks are trial weeks so you can shuffle around courses there which I highly recommend.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went okay. I was lucky during my first quarter that what I ended up taking was open in week 2.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register early! The good courses go quickly. Furthermore, try to time your classes, so you only have to be on campus twice a week. Use the free movement in the first two weeks to find what you like.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Undergrad courses from year 2-4. Most courses are pretty easy and geared towards memorization of specific syllabus stuff.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different and geared towards memorization. All tests are by hand and mostly without notes. Finals are buzzword bingo where they are just looking for specific words and concepts. You are not really encouraged to think by yourself a lot. I had 1 course which was a project exam over the entire 10 weeks, and that worked really well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLI 142A - United States Foreign Policy
POLI 175 - Machine Learning/Social Sciences
POLI 176 - Text as Data
POLI 124A - Pol Conseq/Electoral Systems
POLI 140D - It'l Human Rights Law Migrants
POLI 145C - Interntnl Reltations After Cold War

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
POLI 176 and POLI 175. They are taught with learning in mind and taught interactively via use of assignments and code alongs. Profs are experienced and competent. 
Be aware that softer poli sci courses are taught by lecture style only with very little interactive learning and little else than just reading.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive even when you live off of basic groceries. Regarding housing, bills for water, electrical and heating are not included in the base rent.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive. Going out is fairly priced. Recreation such as the Zoo or museums are very expensive too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Social life is NOT a big thing at UCSD but San Diego in general is great.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a few different clubs at school, but you are not introduced to them by the school, you have to find them for yourself. I found activities away from school instead.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surf! Go to surf school somewhere and find friends through sports such as volleyball, soccer, basketball or (like me) beach handball. Hiking is also very big and there are a lot of beautiful nature around!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Surfing, hiking, exploring, sleeping in the desert. Trying Mexican food. Go watch baseball, watch basketball. Find small neighborhoods.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: No difficulties at all. The American culture is well known, so I knew what to expect.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is very hard to get to know people at UCSD. Most people wake up, go to class, and then go back home. Find other international students, it can give you a nice base!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Americans talk A LOT and often they'll say things they don't mean: "We should totally go surfing next week" and then you don't hear from them in 5 months. You have to contact people and drive the social interactions, if you do not, no one will notice you and help you out of loneliness. 
Also, Americans are VERY loud in public, which takes some getting used to. They do not do it to be rude, that's just how they are.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the sun, the chill vibe around the beach and surf culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the quarter structure - I did 40 ECTS points because of it, and we had very little breaks.
Bring money - California is awesome, but only if you can afford to do things like renting a car or seeing atractions.
Be prepared for sketchy people - a lot of homeless and not-well people live there, and things such as public transportation can be scary.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Please, be prepared for going to school from start Jan to mid June with few breaks. If you wanna take trips and explore, you can do it during the quarters without dying, but do it in the start of a quarter or after the midterms, they are not as intense there. 
Be aware of how important attendence is in your course.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to live on the beach and learn a new culture and skill!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Homesickness, loneliness and expenses

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Look for an American university with semesters - quarter structure means that you have to take 40 ECTS, go to school often and have to be there for app. 6 months which is a long time.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
